subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Sigiriya: The Lion Rock Fortress
description: A micro-lesson that makes Sigiriya: The Lion Rock Fortress usable.

hook.text: A king built his palace on top of a 600-foot rock in Sri Lanka after murdering his own father for the throne.

buildup.text: King Kashyapa I built Sigiriya around 477 CE with gardens, pools, and frescoes painted on the rock face.

discovery.text: The entrance was carved as a giant lion — visitors walked through its open jaws to reach the summit.

twist.text: When his brother returned with an army, Kashyapa rode his war elephant into a swamp and killed himself.

climax.text: The fortress became a Buddhist monastery. Monks added graffiti that is now the oldest surviving writing in Sinhalese.

punchline.text: A murdered king's fortress became a place of peace.

quiz.question: What happened to Sigiriya after King Kashyapa's death?
options: His brother demolished it completely as revenge
It became a Buddhist monastery with ancient graffiti
It was used as a military fort for the next 500 years
